blocks.text: ROMAN EMPEROR · BETWEEN THE TESTAMENTS
Augustus. The emperor whose decree sent Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.
RULEDi
Not given 27 BC – AD 14 (dates vary)
SEAT
Rome
HOUSE
Not stated 2nd of 17 in Rome
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“There went out a decree from Cæsar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed.”
PROPHETS
None named
ROME: 17 RULERS HEROD THE GREAT → PORCIUS FESTUS
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"There went out a decree from Cæsar Augustus, that all the world should be taxed." Luke 2:1
Under that decree "all went to be taxed, every one into his own city", and Joseph went up from Nazareth to Bethlehem with Mary, where Jesus was born. Luke 2:3–7
Luke dates the decree by a governor: "this taxing was first made when Cyrenius was governor of Syria". Luke 2:2
THE SEAT
Rome, where he sat
Seat of the emperors; Luke 2 does not name it
TRIALS AND HEARINGS
The hearings held
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did

From the textMatthew places Jesus' birth "in the days of Herod the king", and Luke opens with "the days of Herod, the king of Judæa". Neither says how Herod stood toward Augustus. Matthew 2:1 Luke 1:5
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · 28 BC, 8 BC AND AD 14
Augustus's own record of his censuses
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · AD 14
Suetonius on his death
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
None. Luke names him once and gives no years (Luke 2:1).
ROMAN RECORDS

Given the title Augustus by decree of the senate for what he did in his sixth and seventh consulships; Shipley dates the decree 16 January 27 BC (Res Gestae 34, with Shipley's note); died 19 August AD 14, 'just thirty-five days before his seventy-sixth birthday' (Suetonius, Augustus 100).
A system of periodic enrolments begun by Augustus
W. M. Ramsay (1898)

From the enrolment papyri of Egypt, Ramsay argued for enrolments by households at regular intervals under Augustus, the first in Syria falling about 8 BC and delayed in Herod's kingdom until about 6 BC. Luke 2:1–3 [20]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Luke 2
PASSAGES · 1
Luke 2:1–7
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say what the enrolment was for, beyond being "taxed" (Luke 2:1-3).
Scripture names no other act of Augustus.
Scripture does not say whether the whole empire was enrolled at the same time.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

From the textLuke 2:1 is the only verse that names Augustus. The site's person record (from STEP Bible) also lists Luke 3:1, which names Tiberius Caesar, Acts 25:21 and 25, where 'Augustus' is used of the emperor reigning when Festus governed, and Acts 27:1, 'Augustus' band', the name of a cohort. Luke 2:1 Luke 3:1 Acts 25:21 Acts 25:25 Acts 27:1

Scholars' viewGill (1746-48) explains 'Augustus' in Acts 25:21 as a title used of the reigning emperor, whom he takes to be Nero; Ellicott's commentary gives three explanations of the cohort's name in Acts 27:1. Acts 25:21 Acts 27:1 [7][3]
